newsitem.title: UK: Abbey still hoping to persuade ScotAm.
newsitem.headline: Abbey still hoping to persuade ScotAm.

text.p: Abbey National is still hoping to persuade the board of mutually-owned life assurance company Scottish Amicable that it should accept Abbey's offer, Abbey deputy chief executive Charles Toner told Reuters.

The offer would provide ScotAm policyholders with an immediate payment worth 400 million stg in either cash or shares and Abbey would also pay between 700 million and 1.0 billion stg into the funds of ScotAm.

"We feel that we can offer something much more attractive to the Scottish Amicable policy holders," Toner said. "That's why we really want to talk to Scottish Amicable and we hope still to persuade them to put this more attractive deal to their policy holders."

Scottish Amicable said the Abbey had not explained its offer sufficiently and that it would pursue its original plan to de-mutualise the company with a view to a stockmarket flotation in three to five years time.
Toner said that the ScotAm board had not yet had time to stand back and examine the proposals properly.

"They've been working on their scheme for some time and they probably can't consider anything else in their minds," he added. "In truth, they don't seem to want to discuss it at the moment but we hope that they will. -- Joe Ortiz, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
